papers.title_in_file: Can Entanglement-enhanced Quantum Kernels Improve Data Classification?
papers.version_note: arXiv:2406.01948v1 preprint dated 4 June 2024. The record id says 2025; the file is the June 2024 preprint.
sections_read: A. Fabrication and Characterization of the Sensor
C. Development of Machine Learning and Quantum Machine Algorithms

figures.shows: Conceptual flow of the QSVM: a data space (x in R^n, database icon) is mapped by phi_Q: x to |psi(x)> into a 'quantum kernel' cloud labelled kappa(x,x') = |<psi(x)|psi(x')>|^2, then to a 'quantum measurement' stage labelled <psi|M|psi>. No numerical data.
figures.confirmed_by: Visual representation illustrating the conceptual flow of the Quantum Support Vector Machine (QSVM).

figures.shows: (a) Scatter plot of the respiratory dataset, f1 (x) against f2 (y), two classes C1 (blue) and C2 (red), heavily intermixed. (b) Scatter plot of the breast cancer dataset, f1 against f2, two classes in two visibly separated bands (green above, orange below). (c) 2-qubit circuit: q0 and q1 each get H then a P(pi/4) phase gate, a controlled phase gate P(-3pi/16) links them, and both qubits are measured into a classical register.
figures.confirmed_by: A quantum circuit of 2 qubits comprising the two Hadamard gates to create the entanglement and two ploy x-gates has been utilized

figures.shows: (a) Scatter plot of the Iris dataset, f1 against f2, three classes (blue, red, teal) with no axis units. (b) Line plot of training accuracy (y, about 0.8 to 1) against circuit depth (x, 0 to about 10): the curve rises from about 0.96 at the lowest depth to about 0.98 near depth 5 and stays flat to depth 10. (c) 4-qubit circuit (q0 to q3) with Hadamard and phase gates, chained controlled-phase gates and four measurements.
figures.confirmed_by: The quantum circuit learning journey shows an increase in the training accuracy as the depth of the circuit increases

figures.shows: (a) Alluvial/Sankey diagram linking kernel (Linear, Poly, Radial, Sigmoid) to learning rate (0.5, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 1E-4) to train accuracy nodes (57, 53, 50, 80, 58, 48, 45) to test accuracy nodes (50, 30, 40, 60). (b) Grouped bar chart of Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1 (y, 0 to 1) for six series: SVM-i, QSVM-i, SVM-r, QSVM-r, SVM-b, QSVM-b. SVM-r (classical, respiratory) is about 0.4 on accuracy and recall and about 0.38 on precision and F1, while QSVM-r is about 0.9 to 0.92. The iris and breast cancer bars are all about 0.9 to 0.97 for both classical and quantum. No error bars.
figures.confirmed_by: The evaluation metrics for training the classical and quantum algorithms have indicated that there is not much deviation in accuracy when training the linear data

papers.what_it_is: A small empirical preprint comparing a Qiskit QSVM with a fidelity quantum kernel against a classical SVM on a self-collected piezoelectric respiratory dataset, the breast cancer dataset and the Iris dataset, claiming 45% higher accuracy on the respiratory data.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QSVM with the entanglement-enhanced kernel performed with 45 % higher accuracy than the classical SVM on the respiratory dataset and almost comparable performance on the breast cancer dataset.
quotes: The QSVM enhanced with the kernel has been found to perform more accurately with 45 % higher accuracy for the randomly acquired respiratory dataset
while providing almost comparable performance for the separate classes of the breast cancer dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single empirical study with no error bars, repeated runs or sample sizes; the text does not say whether 45% is a relative or absolute difference.
assertions.reader_inference: Fig. 4b shows about 0.4 (classical) against about 0.9 (quantum) accuracy on the respiratory data, a gap of about 0.5 absolute, so the 45% figure is not clearly traceable to the plotted values. The abstract also says 'higher accuracy 45%' while the Introduction says '45% higher precision'.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that empirical analysis across diverse datasets shows KQ-SVM significantly outperforms classical SVMs, achieving over 45% higher accuracy on complex datasets while keeping comparable performance on linear datasets.
quotes: Empirical analysis across diverse datasets shows KQ-SVM significantly outperforms classical SVMs
achieving over 45% higher accuracy on complex datasets while maintaining comparable performance on linear datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: Author conclusion resting on one small set of experiments; 'significantly' is not backed by any statistical test in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The 'complex' dataset is only the authors' own respiratory data; no statistical test, confidence interval or repetition is reported.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 4b: on the respiratory dataset the classical SVM (SVM-r) has accuracy of about 0.4 and the QSVM (QSVM-r) about 0.9. Precision, recall and F1 show the same pattern, with SVM-r about 0.38 to 0.4 and QSVM-r about 0.9 to 0.92.
quotes: The summary table of the different evaluation metrics.
while for the random datasets, quantum machine learning performs better with higher accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a bar chart with no error bars; one run.
assertions.reader_inference: The classical respiratory score of about 0.4 is low for a two-class problem; the classical SVM here may be poorly tuned (see the TensorFlow-based implementation).

assertions.value: Read from Figure 4b: on the Iris and breast cancer datasets, classical and quantum models score about the same. Accuracy is about 0.97 for both SVM-i and QSVM-i, about 0.96 for SVM-b and about 0.93 for QSVM-b.
quotes: there is not much deviation in accuracy when training the linear data
The summary table of the different evaluation metrics.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read from a bar chart by eye; single run, no uncertainty.
assertions.reader_inference: The QSVM gives no advantage on the Iris and breast cancer datasets; the advantage is claimed only on the authors' respiratory data. The paper calls Iris 'linear' data in the Fig. 4b discussion, which is not argued.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation metrics show not much deviation in accuracy between classical and quantum algorithms for the linear data.
quotes: there is not much deviation in accuracy when training the linear data
assertions.certainty_reason: Single empirical comparison, no error bars.

assertions.value: The authors state that a 2-qubit circuit with two Hadamard gates (to create entanglement) and two 'ploy x-gates' (as written) was used for the quantum measurement on both the respiratory and the breast cancer datasets.
quotes: A quantum circuit of 2 qubits comprising the two Hadamard gates to create the entanglement and two ploy x-gates has been utilized
to perform the quantum measurement of both datasets (Figure 2c).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its experimental setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Fig. 2c shows H and P(pi/4) on each qubit and a controlled phase gate, which looks like a ZZFeatureMap-style circuit, while the Methods call the entanglement 'CNOT' based (Eq. 6). The paper does not show that the entanglement is what produces the gain, and no non-entangled quantum kernel is tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum model uses Qiskit's ZZFeatureMap, a FidelityQuantumKernel and a QSVC, and that a classical SVC from scikit-learn was trained for comparison.
quotes: feature mapping using the ZZFeatureMap from Qiskit
a fidelity quantum kernel implemented using the Fidelity Quantum Kernel from Qiskit Machine Learning, and the QSVC model for training and classification tasks.
For comparison, we trained a classical Support Vector Classifier (SVC) using scikit-learn.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own description of its implementation.
assertions.reader_inference: The Methods name a ZZFeatureMap while the Results describe a Hadamard plus phase-gate circuit. A fidelity kernel is used, and Eq. 12 is the same fidelity form as the non-entangled Eq. 7. The paper gives no test that separates an entanglement effect.

assertions.value: The authors describe the classical SVM as built with NumPy, TensorFlow and Matplotlib on sequential data, with one-hot encoded labels, an 80% training and 20% testing split, 10 epochs, batch size 32, categorical crossentropy loss and the Adam optimizer.
quotes: Support vector machine (SVM) has been built using Python libraries, including (NumPy, TensorFlow, and Matplotlib), and sequential data for a classification task.
split the data set into 80% training and 20% testing.
It was trained for 10 epochs with batch size 32, using categorical crossentropy loss and the Adam optimizer.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own description of the classical baseline setup.
assertions.reader_inference: A TensorFlow model trained by epochs, batch size and Adam with categorical crossentropy is a neural-network style classifier, not a kernel SVM. The baseline is therefore not clearly a tuned classical SVM, which weakens the classical-versus-quantum comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum model's data were split 80:20 into training and testing sets with stratified sampling and a fixed random seed, and that the quantum measurements were carried out on an IBM platform.
quotes: split the data set into training and testing sets with an 80:20 ratio using stratified sampling.
All the quantum measurements have been carried out on the IBM
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its protocol.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper gives no device name, shot count, noise handling or number of runs, so it is unclear whether results are from hardware or a simulator.

assertions.value: The authors state that the respiratory dataset was acquired with a piezoelectric sensor, in non-invasive mode on the author and volunteers.
assertions.anchor: Section I, p.1; Section V.B, p.5
quotes: classify the random dataset of different breathings acquired by the piezoelectric sensor.
All the measurements were acquired in the non-invasive mode on the author himself and volunteers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of how its dataset was collected.
assertions.reader_inference: No sample count, number of subjects or class definition is given for the respiratory data. The sensor section also mentions both nylon-11 and a PVDF solution, an inconsistency. Fig. 2a shows the two classes heavily overlapping in the two plotted features.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Wisconsin Breast Cancer (Diagnostic) dataset comes from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and was treated as a linear dataset with distinguishable classes.
assertions.anchor: Section V.C.1, p.6; Section III, p.4
quotes: The Wisconsin Breast Cancer (Diagnostic) dataset is obtained from the UCI Machine Learning Repository.
The breast cancer dataset has been taken as a linear dataset, where the two classes are distinguishable (Figure 2(b)).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own description of its data.

assertions.value: The paper defines the entanglement-enhanced quantum kernel as the squared magnitude of the inner product of two entangled feature states |phi_q,e(x)>, where U_e(x) is an entanglement based on the input x.
quotes: Where Ue(x) is an entanglement based on the input x.
Kq,e(xi, xj ) = |⟨ϕq,e(xi)|ϕq,e(xj )⟩|2
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of its kernel (Eqs. 11 and 12).
assertions.reader_inference: The form of U_e(x) is never given, so the kernel is not specified well enough to reproduce or to tell from the plain fidelity kernel of Eq. 7.

assertions.value: The authors attribute the higher accuracy of the quantum SVM to entangled quantum states mapping data to a much higher-dimensional space than classical or non-entangled quantum mappings.
quotes: The higher accuracy of the quantum SVM is attributed to the entangled quantum states effectively mapping data to a much higher-dimensional space compared to classical or nonentangled quantum mappings
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as an explanation with no ablation or test in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: No non-entangled quantum kernel is run, so the paper does not test this attribution. Its title question is therefore not isolated by the experiments.

assertions.value: The abstract states that quantum machine learning algorithms offer significant advantages, including exponentially faster computations.
quotes: quantum machine learning algorithms offer significant advantages, including exponentially faster computations
assertions.certainty_reason: General claim made without evidence in the paper; no run-time measurement is reported.
assertions.reader_inference: The experiments report accuracy only and no timing or complexity analysis, so the speed claim is untested here.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the kernel and learning-rate test the RBF kernel with learning rate 0.01 had the highest training accuracy of 80% but the lowest test accuracy of 30%, which they read as potential overfitting.
quotes: the RBF kernel with a learning rate of 0.01 exhibited the highest accuracy of 80% on the training data but the lowest accuracy
of 30% on the testing data
assertions.certainty_reason: Single run of a small kernel sweep; no repetition or uncertainty.
assertions.reader_inference: A learning rate is not a normal hyperparameter of a kernel SVM, consistent with the neural-style classical baseline. The sweep does not say which dataset was used.

assertions.value: The authors report that the linear kernel with learning rate 0.5 had the best test accuracy of 60% but a lower training accuracy of 57%, which they read as potential underfitting.
quotes: In contrast, the linear kernel with a learning rate of 0.5 achieved the best performance on the test data with an accuracy of 60%
However, it showed a lower accuracy of 57% in the training data
assertions.certainty_reason: Single run of a small kernel sweep, no repetition.
assertions.reader_inference: Test accuracy above training accuracy at these levels suggests a very small test set and noisy estimates.

assertions.value: The authors report that the polynomial kernel reached 53% precision on training data and 50% on test data, and the sigmoid kernel 48% accuracy on training data and 40% on test data.
quotes: the polynomial kernel achieving 53% precision on the training data and 50% in the testing data
the sigmoid kernel achieving 48% accuracy on the training data and 40% on the testing data
assertions.certainty_reason: Single run of a small kernel sweep, no repetition.
assertions.reader_inference: The text mixes 'precision' and 'accuracy' for the same kind of table entry.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 3b: on the Iris dataset the training accuracy of the quantum circuit rises from about 0.96 at the lowest depth to about 0.98 near depth 5 and stays flat to depth 10.
quotes: Training accuracy vs depth plot.
The quantum circuit learning journey shows an increase in the training accuracy as the depth of the circuit increases
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a line plot; training accuracy only, single run.
assertions.reader_inference: The rise is small (about 0.02) and only training accuracy is shown, so it does not show better generalization.

assertions.value: The authors state that the increased training accuracy in Figure 3b prompts further investigation to confirm whether it indicates successful information extraction or potential overfitting.
quotes: The increased accuracy in Figure 3b prompts further investigation to confirm whether it indicates successful information extraction or potential overfitting.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the caveat on their own measured depth result (training accuracy only).

assertions.value: The authors state that the Iris dataset (3 classes) was classified with a 4-qubit circuit using Hadamard gates to create entanglement.
quotes: we have utilized the Iris dataset having 3 classes.
The 4-qubit quantum circuit consists of a 4hadammard gate to create the entanglement (Figure 3c).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its setup.
assertions.reader_inference: This 4-qubit Iris circuit differs from the 2-qubit circuit used for the two main datasets, and the Iris quantum result in Fig. 4b is not linked to either one.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Iris scatter plot in Figure 3a lacks clear labeling, which obscures the specific attributes used for classification and makes precise interpretation difficult.
quotes: the lack of clear labeling obscures the specific attributes used for classification, making precise interpretations difficult to find.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit on their own figure.
